resources.evidence_note: Sections 4–5: 50 unseen test users versus 1,000 training users; experts judge histories. Dispersion acts on adapter outputs. Code uses 30 x 1024 user parameters and prompt-dependent, block-specific text modulation. The preference offset does not read the current latent or actual timestep, while native FLUX modulation remains timestep-dependent. New-user coefficients are optimized; the released linear configuration does not impose a convex combination. Appendix A explicitly discusses diverse preferences within a single PIP user; this is not evidence that one user embedding forces a unimodal output distribution.
resources.limitations: Expert judgments are not votes from the target users. Eight adaptation examples and twenty evaluation samples per test user do not alone certify global prompt-disjointness.

resources.evidence_note: Sections 3-4: frozen SDXL, session GP posterior fitting and inference-time attention-warp search. Human feedback drives the main loop; reward-based variants replace it. Thirty external volunteers rank target similarity; they are not established as thirty target users.
resources.limitations: Specific target reconstruction, not persistent taste transfer. No diffusion-weight tuning; whether GP hyperparameters are refitted per user remains unverified, hence unclear for parameter optimization. Four choices and up to fifty rounds; no verified held-out-user/prompt protocol.
